Introduction  
Artificial intelligence (AI) research has expanded from symbolic reasoning to adaptive systems that perceive, infer, and act. This paper studies how layered design choices shape the behavior of modern AI. We define the analytic unit, notated as AI (model (architecture (component (interface (core [subsystem {module} subsystem] core) interface) component) architecture) model) and use it to compare learning, perception, and planning. The central question is how nested dependencies across components affect reliability, interpretability, and governance. Our contribution is threefold: (1) we propose a modular taxonomy for AI systems; (2) we evaluate the role of layered interfaces in system performance; and (3) we outline implications for transparent, accountable deployment. By making the nested structure explicit, the paper aims to improve comparative analysis of AI architectures.
